headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of data leakage, prompt injection, and cascading mistakes between kotaemon and Mentat.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, chat transcripts, and files in ./ktem_app_data, while Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem. That creates a default path for attacker-controlled content from one agent to influence the other through shared files, even without MCP or clipboard bridges.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory tree or exchanged files are opened by Mentat, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF Kotaemon indexes untrusted HTML/MHTML or chat transcripts that Mentat later reads, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent's working files.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted HTML/MHTML and transcripts.
Require manual review before Mentat opens any Kotaemon-generated file.
Prefix shared files with a non-executable format like plain text summaries.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels and content filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon handles API keys and broad document classes, and Mentat can read/write the filesystem with broad network egress. If they share a workspace, Mentat can read sensitive files that Kotaemon stores or processes, and either agent can transmit contents to external model APIs by default.
conditions: IF Kotaemon stores API keys or sensitive documents in ./ktem_app_data and Mentat can read that path, leakage is reachable.
IF either agent sends file contents to a configured model provider, sensitive data can leave the local machine.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate OS user or container.
Move secrets out of any shared workspace immediately.
Restrict Mentat to a narrow allowlist of files.
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Kotaemon also uses a local data directory and supports multiple instances. Their overlapping write surfaces can race on shared files or repositories, but the profiles do not show unrestricted same-directory git writes by both agents, so this is below high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or data directory, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF Mentat commits or rewrites files that Kotaemon also updates, state corruption becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories.
Pause one agent while the other writes shared files.
Use git branches per agent.
Review diffs before applying them.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kotaemon produces retrieved answers, citations, and chat transcripts that Mentat could treat as input for edits. Mentat then proposes multi-file diffs. Without an explicit verification step, errors or hallucinated facts from Kotaemon can cascade into incorrect code changes or documentation edits.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes Kotaemon output as authoritative text, unverified claims can propagate into edits.
IF Kotaemon returns a wrong citation or summary and Mentat applies it, downstream mistakes become persistent.
mitigations: Require Mentat to verify every factual claim against source files.
Keep Kotaemon outputs in a review-only buffer.
Ask for a second-pass human check before applying diffs.
Limit Mentat to small, reversible patches.
requires-engineering: add structured provenance checks between retrieval and editing.

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document classes, while Mentat processes source code and sends content to a configured model provider. If regulated or confidential data is placed in the shared workflow, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches, but the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdictional breach.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are routed through both agents, retention and access controls must align.
IF the configured model provider stores prompts outside the required jurisdiction, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared pair workflow.
Confirm provider retention settings before use.
Separate secret-handling tasks from coding tasks.
Document which agent may process which data class.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement.
